title: All-Hands July 2026 - Announcement + Q&A Draft
content:
Goal: Draft the opening announcement and a compact Q&A for the July 2026 company all-hands. This is my working copy - lots of TODOs and rough phrasing.

High-level message (30-45s):
- Opening: Quick thanks for a solid Q2 - hitting important infra and product milestones that set us up for the second half.
- Theme: 'Serving in production' - call out our focus on reliability and cost-for-performance as the differentiator this year.
- Highlights to call out: Dedicated GA improvements, Private deployment pilot wins, Redwood Optimize early customer results (30-40% cost improvements for two customers), new observability features shipped in Console.
- Closing line: Preview of what's next - focus on scale, reliability, and enterprise readiness (more regions, more private deployments, SLAs).

Draft opener (verbatim candidate):
"Hi everyone - thanks for joining. Quick call-out to the engineering and product teams: the last quarter was a heavy lift across Dedicated capacity, Private pilots, and Console observability, and it shows. Today I want to focus on how those efforts translate to reliability, predictable economics, and better experiences for customers building on Redwood. We'll cover wins, where we're investing next, and a few pragmatic asks for the org as we scale."

Top bullets to surface in the all-hands slides (for speaker):
- Product: Dedicated latency SLO improvements (p99 down 15-20ms), Private pilot: 2 regulated customers onboarded, GA of new rollout policies.
- Platform/Runtime: New kernel selection rollout to prod across A100 clusters, reduced tail latency for long-context workflows.
- Optimize: Initial recommendations feature led to 28-35% token-cost reduction for two pilot customers.
- Console/Observability: Token-level cost heatmaps, per-route tracing, and alerting for regression detection now live.
- People ops: Hires in SRE and Applied ML incoming (brief hiring ask).

Q&A - Likely questions and suggested responses (short):
Q: Any update on pricing for hosted API?
A: No immediate price change. We continue to tune unit economics and will announce any pricing changes with at least 30 days notice and clear migration guidance. Focus right now is tooling to give customers control over cost (Optimize recommendations, batching defaults).

Q: When will Private be generally available?
A: Private is in pilot with a few regulated customers; GA target is H2 2026. We need more pilot feedback on networking/KMS integration and the on-prem install experience before broad GA.

Q: Why are we doing Dedicated vs Public hosted - what's the differentiation?
A: Dedicated is for predictable throughput and data isolation (reserved GPU pools, SLA-backed). Hosted remains the fastest onboarding path for most customers. We're investing in both - routing policies let us move requests based on cost/latency/region.

Q: Can you say more about reliability/regression detection?
A: Console now exposes per-route regression alerts tied to prompt sets; we are also shipping automatic fallback policies for model variants when capacity is constrained. From an SLO perspective, we're tracking p50/p95/p99 across routes and surfacing trends in the console.

Unresolved items / TODOs (please review):
- Exact phrasing for Dedicated SLA numbers - need confirmation from legal/finance. (Action: Maya to confirm SLA matrix by 2026-06-30.)
- Private GA timing - product to confirm H2 roadmap commitment. (Priya owning update.)
- One-liner and keynote quote for the CEO - request draft from Asha.
- Add a short customer testimonial (if we get explicit ok from pilot customers).

Logistics notes for speaker run: I plan to run the deck Friday AM with product and SRE leads. We should keep the main talk to 18 minutes, then 12 minutes for Q&A. Suggest parking long technical questions to the post-all-hands deep-dive sessions.

Tone guidance for final draft: Empathetic, engineering-first, avoid marketing hyperbole. Call out concrete numbers and what we learned. Use 'we' language. Keep ask of the company simple and actionable (e.g., file tickets for immediate regressions, join the post-show SRE drop-in).

Fallback lines (short):
- If asked about layoffs/budget: 'No org-wide reductions planned - our focus is allocation of resources to highest-impact areas (reliability and private deployments).'
- If asked about open-source model support: 'We'll continue to expand curated model catalog and share performance guidance for top open models; customers can pin versions for stability.'

Notes-to-self formatting reminders:
- Remove all bracketed TODOs before sending to comms.
- Double-check Confluence link and add one-line customer quote if available.
- Share final script with CEO and product leads 48 hours before all-hands.

Quick copy for in-email announcement (short):
Subject: All-Hands - July 2026 update (Wed 10am PT)
Body (first sentence): Join us for the July all-hands where we'll share product and platform progress, pilot wins in Private, Dedicated performance improvements, and what's next as we scale for enterprise customers. Bring questions - we'll have 12 minutes of live Q&A and follow-up drop-in sessions.

End - please add edits inline or DM for quick calls.

- 2026-06-30: updated timeline and TODO list after hiring sync.
